page.layout: One column of running text on one printed page. Top: running head and page number. Below, the body of the column, with a heading-like section mark "§. IX." at the upper right. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: DD. Proff. Lyd. loc. cit. th. 46. Et sunt in se considerati mandatarii meri, qui proprii nihil habent, quod est argumentum Amesii. Et ut F. Junius loquitur de hac re lib.4.c.16. Potestas Ecclesiastica est ministerii potius, quàm potestatis, nec citra rationem decori & honestatis quicquam in Ecclesia potest. Item ibid. Ecclesiastica potestas est ministerium non potestas αὐτο-κρατορικὴ[?] ut Magistratus. II. Quia consequenter etiam ministris non competit potestas coactiva externa. Unde non possunt judicium ferre, quando quæstio est de incarceratione, exilio, multâ pecuniariâ aut ullâ pœna corporali. Vide P. Martyrem Loc. communib. Cl. IV. c, 13. §. 9. & Cl. Walæum p. 53. 54. 55. ubi hanc doctrinam contra Concil. Trident. Sess. 25. 3. & contra praxin Episcoporum in Papatu defendit ex verbo Dei, atque inter alia ait p. 54. Ministros ne quidem acceptare debere hanc potestatem à Magistratu, sive vel ma-gumen-[?]

page.notes: The section mark "§. IX." at the upper right is a printed section marker, not part of the running head, so it is not transcribed as one. Greek word "αὐτοκρατορικὴ" is a best reading across a line break ("αὐτο-" / "κρατορικὴ"); the hyphen and accents are uncertain. The last word "magumen-" is broken at the line end with "gumen-" printed right-aligned; the completion is not legible. The paragraph continues onto the next page. The first line "DD. Proff. Lyd." opens the column in the same type as the text and is treated as continuation from the previous page's note.
